findings.issue: Wave 1 runs Task 3 (adds `Group.title` / `Board.groupOrder` to `src/data/types.ts`) in parallel with Task 5 (title resolution) and Task 4 (reorder logic), and both of the latter list `src/data/types.ts` in Files to read. Task 5's stated scope — resolving a group's displayed name "from its stored name and the localized default" — reads `Group.title`, which does not exist until Task 3 lands. Agents in the same wave start from the same base, so Task 5 would be written against a type that lacks the field. No file is modified twice, so there is no merge conflict, and Task 5's verify (`npm test`) would still pass because vitest transpiles without type checking — which is exactly why the mismatch could go unnoticed until Wave 2. Task 4 is lower risk: it operates on `GroupId[]` and `hiddenGroups`, both pre-existing.
findings.fix: Either (a) move Task 3 into Wave 0 (it has no dependency on Tasks 1 or 2 beyond the runtime being usable) and leave Tasks 4 and 5 alone in Wave 1, or (b) state Task 5's signature explicitly as primitives — `(storedTitle: string, defaultLabel: string) => string` — so it carries no dependency on the new model, and drop `src/data/types.ts` from its Files to read.

findings.issue: Rationale clauses still linger in three task descriptions, duplicating content that already lives in Decisions or Risks. Task 2: "which currently makes type checking fail for everyone" (Decision 9). Task 8: "so names and order reach storage together, normalized on the way" (Backward Compatibility → Consumer impact, and the Risks row on partial save-chain updates). Task 9: "which stop being stable once names are editable" (Risks row on popup locators). Much milder than round 1 — these are one-clause justifications, not embedded decisions with alternatives.
findings.fix: Trim to scope: Task 2 — "Also add the translation key left missing by feature 0009"; Task 8 — "Extend the whole save path in one step, normalizing names on the way"; Task 9 — "Move existing scenarios off locating groups and popup rows by displayed names onto the identifiers introduced in the previous waves."

findings.issue: Task 12's `Verify: bash — documentation matches the shipped schema` is not an executable command, and the same text appears in the Per-task verification table (row 12). Task 11 (Pre-deploy QA) has no `Verify:` field at all, although the table assigns it `npm test && npx playwright test && npm run build` — the task body and the table disagree on which tasks carry a verify step.
findings.fix: For Task 12 either give a concrete check (e.g. `grep -n 'groupOrder' docs/technical.md` plus a version-number check) or drop `verify:` entirely, since a documentation edit has no machine-checkable output — and mirror that choice in the table. For Task 11, add the table's command as the task's `Verify:` line so body and table match.

findings.issue: Task 10's description reproduces the E2E scenario list from Testing Strategy almost verbatim in a single sentence (nine scenarios). It reads as a test plan rather than a scope statement, and the duplication means the two lists can drift apart independently. Carried over from round 1, unchanged.
findings.fix: Shorten to scope with a pointer: "Cover the feature end to end per the E2E scenarios listed in Testing Strategy, including dragging a task both ways between reordered groups in the same session without reloading."

findings.issue: Project Knowledge is still absent — `.claude/skills/` does not exist in this repository, so neither `architecture.md` nor `patterns.md` could be read. Standards compliance was therefore checked against CLAUDE.md only, and the tech-spec is consistent with it: new pure modules land in `src/ui/` next to the existing `boardLayoutUtils.ts`, unit tests move to `tests/unit/` (which exists and already holds `migration.test.ts`, `cleanup.test.ts`, `statusTransitions.test.ts`), E2E stays in `tests/e2e/`, and all styling goes to `src/styles.css` rather than scoped `<style>` blocks.
findings.fix: Optional and outside this feature: create the project-knowledge references so future tech-specs are validated against a documented architecture baseline instead of CLAUDE.md alone.

summary: Round 2: the critical wave conflict is resolved and no new critical issues were found — status is approved. Verified fixes: the seven-wave structure (0-6 plus Final Wave) puts each `src/styles.css` writer in its own wave (Task 6 in Wave 2, Task 7 in Wave 3, Task 8 in Wave 4), and no other file is modified by two tasks in the same wave; the attribute-then-locator ordering the Risks table assumes is now encoded (Task 7 Wave 3 and Task 8 Wave 4 introduce the identifiers, Task 9 Wave 5 migrates locators, Task 10 Wave 6 adds new scenarios); the Task 5 scope-vs-files mismatch is gone (title resolution, display and popup are now Tasks 5, 6 and 8 with disjoint file sets); `dev-security-auditor` is present on every code-writing task and on the infrastructure task; task descriptions no longer carry decisions with rationale and alternatives. Template compliance is complete: frontmatter valid (created 2026-08-06, status draft, branch feature/group-customization, size L), all sections present and non-empty including both Architecture subsections, all three Agent Verification Plan subsections, a Risks table with realistic non-generic entries, and Acceptance Criteria; 14 Decisions each carry Decision + Rationale + Alternatives considered; 12 tasks (limit 15); all skills (infrastructure-setup, code-writing, pre-deploy-qa, documentation-writing) and all reviewers exist in the catalog and on disk in ~/.claude/agents/; the Per-task verification table renumbered cleanly to 12 rows and the Risks table's task references (1, 8, 9) now point at the right tasks; the document is time-free, with no line-number references, no AC blocks and no TDD anchors inside tasks. One major finding remains: Wave 1 runs the data-model task in parallel with the title-resolution task that consumes the new field. Four minors are informational. Side check: `npx tsc --noEmit` currently emits exactly two errors, both from the missing `'boardSettings.notes'` key, so Task 2's "clean tsc" verify is achievable.
